- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) and forecast is rising sharply, reduce overshoot by 5–10% to avoid overcorrection.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤ 0.33) and forecast is falling, avoid premature bottoming — maintain slight upward bias to capture rebound.  
- After a spike in price (forecast > 65), model tends to overcorrect downward — apply a 3–5 day lagged mean reversion buffer.  
- When sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and price is trending, model often misreads momentum — align forecast with 3-period moving average of history.  
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome deviates > 2% from 14-day moving average of history, adjust forecast toward historical mean unless sentiment strongly contradicts.  
- If sentiment is consistently positive over 3+ days, model should not forecast sharp declines — expect mean reversion within 5–7 days unless strong macro signal.  
- Overshoots after spikes (forecast > true + 5%) should be capped at +3% of prior peak unless sentiment confirms continuation.  
- When sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67) and price is volatile, forecast should be smoother — use 5-day exponential smoothing to reduce noise.
